title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 312-313 of the 'Longue Marche' sequel): Grothendieck compares the first two 'modular multiplicities' (analytic orbifolds or stacks) of the Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}, and their fundamental groups.

On the previous page he argued, via a gerbe argument, that there is a canonical isomorphism (70) T_{1,1}/{±1} ≅ 𝔖_{0,3}, well defined only modulo inner automorphisms. Here:
- T_{1,1} ≅ GL(2,Z) is the extended Teichmüller (mapping class) group of type (1,1).
- 𝔖_{0,3} is the 'mixed' fundamental group of the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3), where U_{0,3} = P^1 minus 3 points = M_{0,4} and 𝔖_3 permutes the three punctures.

This page opens by noting that because of the inner-automorphism indeterminacy, (70) is only meaningful as a map of 'exterior' (outer) groups. It then gives the geometric source of (70).

The analytic morphism (71) sends an elliptic curve E to the quotient E/{±1} ≅ P^1. This P^1 has one distinguished branch point (the image of 0) and an unordered set of three further branch points (the images of the 2-torsion points). The target is therefore the multiplicity M^an_{1,1} → U^an_{0,3} ≅ M_{0,1+3} ≅ (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3), i.e. the stack quotient [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3]. The marginal comment calls U_{0,3} the 'universal' compact analytic curve of type (0,3).

The map kills exactly the generic automorphism −1. So it induces (72): the rigidification M^an_{1,1}' (M_{1,1} with −1 removed) is isomorphic to this multiplicity. On outer fundamental groups it gives (73): T^+_{1,1} = SL(2,Z) → 𝔖^+_{0,3}, with image PSL(2,Z) ≅ F_2 ⋊ 𝔖_3, i.e. the extension of 𝔖_3 = SL(2,Z/2) by Γ(2)/±1 ≅ π_1(P^1 − 3 pts). This is the Birman–Hilden / Legendre-λ picture.

He then asks whether (73) can be made an actual homomorphism, not just an outer one. His answer begins at the bottom of the page and continues on the next:
- Use the canonical universal cover of M^an_{1,1}, namely Teichmüller space = the Poincaré half-plane D.
- Use the λ-map D → U^an_{0,3}, equivariant along SL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/2) ≅ 𝔖_3.
- This exhibits D as a universal cover of the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3), and SL(2,Z)' as the mixed π_1 relative to that cover.
- The aim is to identify this with π_1((U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3); P = tangential base point), so that the indeterminacy disappears once compatible base points or universal covers are chosen.

The purpose is to set up base-point-precise comparisons between π_1(M_{1,1}) and π_1(M_{0,4}). This is needed for the action of Gal(Q̄/Q) and GT ('variations sur l'équation des lacets') on both levels of the tower.
errors: (72) as transcribed has target M^an_{0,3}, which is a point and cannot be isomorphic to the rigidified M_{1,1}. The intended target must be the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3) = [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3] from (71). This is either a notational slip by Grothendieck or a misreading of the handwriting.

(71) itself is not an isomorphism: the generic stabilizer ±1 of M_{1,1} maps trivially, so M_{1,1} → [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3] is a μ_2-gerbe. Grothendieck correctly passes to the rigidification M_{1,1}' for the isomorphism (72), and to T/±1 for the groups.
No mathematical error in the main line; the identification requires care about which tangential base point on U_{0,3} corresponds to the cusp at i∞ of D. This is left to the next page.

ideas.what: M_{1,1} → [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3] via E ↦ E/±1 with its branch points; the rigidification of M_{1,1} is isomorphic to the 𝔖_3-quotient of P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Legendre λ-map / hyperelliptic quotient; Birman–Hilden correspondence Mod_{1,1}/±1 ≅ Mod_{0,1+3}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre, Jacobi, Klein); Birman–Hilden 1973 for mapping class groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{0,4} and M_{1,1} as the first stage of the Teichmüller tower, but not this explicit comparison in detail

ideas.what: Outer isomorphism SL(2,Z)/±1 ≅ π_1 of the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3), i.e. PSL(2,Z) ≅ F_2 ⋊ 𝔖_3 with F_2 = Γ(2)/±1
ideas.modern_name: PSL(2,Z) as orbifold fundamental group; Γ(2) ↔ π_1(P^1 − 3 pts)

ideas.what: Upgrading outer homomorphisms to genuine ones by using the universal cover D (Teichmüller space) and tangential base points, so that π_1 of M_{1,1} becomes SL(2,Z) on the nose, compatibly with π_1(M_{0,4}, tangential base point)
ideas.modern_name: tangential base points on moduli stacks; GT/Galois action on π_1(M_{1,1}, \vec{∞}) compatible with M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto 1990s-2000s

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful working-out of the classical relation between M_{1,1} and M_{0,4}/𝔖_3 (Legendre / Birman–Hilden) and its effect on fundamental groups. It also poses the natural question of lifting outer maps to genuine ones via the half-plane and tangential base points. All of this is classical or later done explicitly (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Hain–Matsumoto). It is historically interesting as evidence of Grothendieck's attention to base-point-precise comparisons in the Teichmüller tower, but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: First line: likely 'si on le voit seulement comme groupe extérieur' (a verb is missing in the transcription).

(72): the target should be read as the multiplicity (U_{0,3}, 𝔖_3) ≅ [M_{0,4}/𝔖_3] (possibly written with a different decoration), not literally M_{0,3}; and M^an_{1,1}' denotes the rigidified M_{1,1}.
The insertion rendered as '𝔻𝒳' above 'morphisme canonique' is probably an illegible inserted word (e.g. 'de multiplicités'), not a symbol.
The superscript in 'M^{1 an}_{0,4}' is uncertain; it may denote M_{0,1+3} (one marked point plus three unordered points).

The marginal diagonal note is largely illegible. It seems to ask whether one can define a lifting of (73) to a genuine group homomorphism compatible with (70); the transcription's guesses should be treated as tentative.
